papers.title_en: Same Semantics, Different Outcome: On the Modality Robustness of Multimodal LLMs under Knowledge Conflict
papers.authors: Jungyeon Lee, Yejin Yoon, Taeuk Kim
papers.evidence: 研究知识冲突下多模态大模型的模态鲁棒性
papers.tldr: 多模态大模型在处理文本与图像形式相同证据时表现不一致，尤其在证据与参数知识冲突时。研究发现模型更易接受图像形式的矛盾上下文，且图文同时呈现时偏好随机，影响多模态RAG并易受攻击。多数干预无效，监督微调效果中等，呼吁多阶段训练关注此根本性问题。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly provided with contextual evidence in heterogeneous forms: as a text passage, as a rendered image of the same passage, or as both together. However, it remains unclear how consistently these surface forms are processed, especially when the evidence conflicts with the model's parametric knowledge. We study modality robustness under knowledge conflict across 13 MLLMs and two datasets, and find them far from robust. (1) Contrary to common belief, models favor a context that contradicts parametric knowledge more readily in image form than in text form; (2) when a contradicting text and image are presented together, the preferred modality is essentially arbitrary, varying with input order, model, and dataset. We further demonstrate that this instability has practical consequences: it degrades performance in multimodal RAG and can be exploited by adversarial attacks. To alleviate this brittleness, we examine several simple techniques---prompting, steering, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and direct preference optimization; the majority prove ineffective, whereas SFT achieves moderate success. We therefore call for greater awareness of this inconsistency and argue that it is fundamental, demanding attention at multiple training stages.
